candidates.statement: Cancer immunotherapeutic drugs and biological products (hereafter referred to as cancer 10 immunotherapeutic drugs) can modulate (i.e., stimulate or suppress) the endogenous immune 11 system to produce an anticancer effect. Adverse events 2 that are consistent with an autoimmune 12 etiology should be evaluated as potential immune-mediated adverse reactions (imAR) 3 to guide 13 patient management and inform the drug labeling or investigator brochure, as applicable. 14
candidates.context: For the purpose of this guidance, the term imAR refers to adverse reactions that occurred in the 16 context of exposure to a cancer immunotherapeutic drug and are consistent with the development 17 of an autoimmune reaction, and are not attributable to another cause (e.g., infection, trauma, 18 other drugs). While corticosteroids and other immunosuppressive drugs are regularly used to 19 manage imARs in cancer clinical trials, the absence of a history of immunosuppressive treatment 20 for an adverse reaction does not preclude its characterization as an imAR, especially for low- 21 grade imARs that result in dose interruption. 22

candidates.statement: This guidance provides recommendations regarding the data that should be collected and 31 evaluated to assess whether adverse events qualify as imARs and the data on imARs that should 32 be included in a new drug application (NDA) or biologics license application (BLA) for a cancer 33 immunotherapeutic drug. 34
candidates.context: This guidance is intended for sponsors of cancer immunotherapeutic drugs that modulate the 24 endogenous immune system and may disrupt immunologic tolerance to normal organs and 25 tissues. Examples of such cancer immunotherapeutic drugs include monoclonal antibodies, 26 anticancer vaccines, and cytokines. Adoptively transferred cell-based cancer immunotherapeutics 27 that target a tumor-associated antigen (TAA) and directly exert an anticancer effect (e.g., a TAA- 28 directed genetically modified T-cell immunotherapy) are outside the scope of this guidance. 29 The contents of this document do not have the force and effect of law and are not meant to bind 36 the public in any way, unless specifically incorporated into a contract. candidates.statement: Sponsors should develop a prespecified list of potential imARs consisting of groupings of 80 Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) terms describing the same medical 81 concept using all levels of the MedDRA hierarchy including Standardized MedDRA Queries 82 (SMQs) on which data should be collected to characterize a potential imAR. This list should be 83 updated throughout the development program and included in relevant documents (e.g., in the 84 protocol, investigator brochure, safety analysis plan). When developing this list, the sponsor 85 should consider the: 86
candidates.context: A. Identifying Potential imARs 78 • Mechanism of action of the drug and prior experience with the same or similar 88 immunotherapeutics in oncology, as well as other disease settings 89 • Immunologic impact of the cancer or prior cancer therapy. 90

candidates.statement: As an example of immunologic impact of prior cancer therapy, in allogeneic hematopoietic stem 92 cell transplantation (HSCT), multiple non-randomized trials evaluating PD-1 targeted antibodies 93 in patients either before or after undergoing allogeneic HSCT demonstrated an increased risk of 94 transplant related complications, even after PD-1 targeted antibody treatment had been 95 discontinued. Therefore, examples of potential imARs that should be prespecified for data 96 collection in this setting include hyperacute graft versus host disease (GVHD), acute GVHD, 97 chronic GVHD, hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD) after reduced intensity conditioning, and 98 steroid-requiring febrile syndrome (without an identified infectious cause). 99

candidates.statement: In some circumstances, individual case assessment can be clarified by a rechallenge (if 116 appropriate), or follow-up response to immunosuppressive therapy. Causality, however, may not 117 be clear until sufficient exposure reveals an increase in incidence or severity of the specific 118 imAR within the arm of interest. Increased surveillance (e.g., defining the potential imAR as an 119 Adverse Events of Special Interest(AESI)) 4 in subsequent trials for suspected imARs is 120 appropriate to facilitate a causality assessment. In addition, when immunotherapeutic drugs with 121 a mechanism that decreases the threshold for disrupting peripheral immunological tolerance are 122 used in combination with a drug infrequently associated with an organ specific toxicity, a 123 marked increase in the frequency of organ specific toxicity should be considered an imAR until 124 proven otherwise (e.g., evaluate for immune-mediated nephritis rather than attribute to 125 chemotherapy-induced acute renal failure in a patient receiving an immunotherapeutic plus 126 chemotherapy combination regimen). These considerations should also be included in protocols 127 to assist investigators in determining whether there is a reasonable possibility that the drug 128 caused the adverse event. 5 129

candidates.context: This section of the guidance summarizes labeling recommendations on how to incorporate imAR 227 information into the WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS and DOSAGE AND 228 ADMINISTRATION sections of labeling for cancer immunotherapeutic drugs. The 229 recommendations for this section of this guidance are not intended to be exhaustive. Information 230 about imARs may be included in other sections of labeling (e.g., PATIENT COUNSELING 231 1. WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS Section 235

candidates.statement: Clinically significant imARs should be incorporated into one numbered subsection in the 237 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS section of labeling (e.g., 5.1 Severe and Fatal Immune- 238 Mediated Adverse Reactions ). Clinically significant imARs include those that occurred with 239 the subject drug as well as those that occurred with drugs in the same class (e.g., same 240 mechanism of action), as appropriate. When imARs are based on a pooled safety database, to 241 reduce redundancy from providing a detailed description of pooled safety data multiple times in 242 labeling, FDA recommends including this information in the Clinical Trials Experience 243 subsection in the ADVERSE REACTIONS section, instead of the imAR subsection in the 244 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS section. The imAR subsection should cross-reference to 245 the Clinical Trials Experience subsection for the detailed description of pooled safety data. In 246 the imAR subsection in the WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS section, FDA recommends: 247
